Definition: from a derivative of G1199 (equivalent to G1196); a place of bondage, i.e. a dungeon:--prison.
BiblicalUsage: A prison is the place of bondage, and Acts keeps putting God's servants in one. The apostles are shut in the common prison and freed by an angel, the Philippian jail shakes open at midnight, and John the Baptist hears of Christ's works from his own cell.
TheologicalSignificance: I believe the prisons in Acts prove that no door can shut the gospel in. Angels open them, earthquakes shake them, and even a prophet in chains can still send his disciples to ask Christ who He is.
RelatedEvents: Paul and Silas in the Philippian Prison
